questions.question: For AlxCoCrFeNi HEAs in the high-stress regime (σ > threshold) at ≤600 °C, does increasing the Al content shift the dominant mechanism from dislocation climb-precipitate interaction to grain-boundary sliding, thereby reducing the stress exponent below 8.9?
questions.rationale: Determining if Al content alters the deformation mechanism is critical for designing high-stress creep-resistant HEAs, as the current model assumes a fixed mechanism of climb and precipitation.
questions.decision_use: If the mechanism shifts, alloy composition must be adjusted to stabilize precipitates or grain boundaries; if not, Al content can be optimized solely for precipitate volume fraction.
answer_requirements: Measure stress exponents and activation energy for AlxCoCrFeNi with varying Al (x=0.15 to 1.0) at 550-600 °C
Perform TEM to identify dislocation configurations and precipitate morphology at high stress
Correlate the stress exponent values with the presence/absence of dynamic recrystallization and grain boundary sliding signatures
evidence_spans: It should be pointed out that the testing temperatures were up to 750–900 °C and far beyond the softening temperature (~600 °C) of the investigated alloys [ [19] ]. From a scientific view, the strain-rate-jump or stress increment test method is inadequate using a single specimen at respective temperatures, as the microstructure during elevated-temperature plastic flow is generally not invariant.
However, this value is still higher than those for traditional solid solution alloys, which implies that the sole recrystallization is insufficient
the abnormally high stress exponents in HSR were ascribed to the coordinative contributions of dynamic recrystallization and dynamic precipitation
